report: Week 10 is a hard spot at 2-7, but the lineup is mostly healthy. Rhamondre Stevenson is the only alert: he is questionable, but he has the best matchup on the roster (DET gives up the 30th-most to RBs, 16.43 last-3 average), so he stays in. Woody Marks is the backup if he's ruled out. I checked every bench-for-starter swap and the lineup is already set, so there are no start/sit changes. Tee Higgins is on fire (28.17 last-3), but Stafford faces ARI, which allows the 2nd-fewest points to QBs, and he is averaging only 12.33 over his last three. QB is the biggest upgrade spot. Send the Tetairoa McMillan + Tank Dell offer for Christian Watson first, then the Stroud offer for the QB spot.

team_breakdown.note: Stafford averages 15.87 (12.33 last-3) with a 9.12 floor, and ARI is a tough draw. Several teams have a better QB sitting on their bench.
Javonte Williams is a true lead back (17.73 average, 23 carries). White (9.74) and Stevenson (12.63, questionable) are only average behind him.
Higgins averages 19.98 (28.17 last-3) and McMillan 15.56, but McMillan has slipped to 11.8 over his last three.
LaPorta averages 11.64 but only 5.5 over his last three. His matchup is good (NE gives up the 26th-most to TEs), but he has been inconsistent.
Jameson Williams is the steady piece (13.21 average, 16.03 last-3, 83% snaps). Stevenson is the other flex and carries an injury tag.
Flournoy (9.31) and Marks (8.86) are usable. McConkey is hurt and slumping (5.1 last-3), and Black, McGowan, Strong and Knight can't help a lineup.

plan: Upgrade QB to a 19-20+ average starter (Stroud or Josh Allen).
Add a true WR1/WR2 such as Christian Watson (19.66 average, MIN allows the 30th-most points to WRs) in place of McMillan.
Use bench depth to add a steadier RB2/FLEX and clear the dead roster spots.

replacements.why: One-game risk; Marks has 17 carries a game and an 8.28 floor.

drops.why: Third-string back with no stats and nothing to start over.
3.63 average on 31% snaps; nothing to start him over.

trades.why: Christian Watson averages 19.66 (19.37 last-3) with an 8.67 targets-per-game load, and MIN gives up the 30th-most points to WRs. That is MORE POINTS: +4.1 over McMillan's 15.56 average, and +7.6 on the last-3 numbers. TWILL4 gets McMillan, who is nearly as good, and Dell (13 average) to replace Konata Mumpfield, who is starting at 4.15, so they come out ahead overall.
trades.opener: McMillan for Watson straight up, see what he asks for.
trades.fallback: Add Flournoy to the offer; walk away if he wants Higgins.
trades.text: Sent you a WR swap, take a look when you can.

trades.why: C.J. Stroud averages 20.51 (24.95 last-3) with a 16.48 floor, against Stafford's 15.87 and 9.12. That is MORE POINTS and MORE RELIABLE at QB. Zane already starts Jayden Daniels (19.42), so Stroud is a spare for him, and Williams (13.21) replaces Germie Bernard (9.54) as his WR3, a gain of about 3.7. Tank Dell (13 average) steps into my flex, so I lose almost nothing there.
trades.fallback: Add Flournoy for a WR depth piece; walk away if he asks for Higgins.
trades.text: Sent a QB for WR offer, let me know.

trades.why: Josh Allen averages 25.09 with a 17.8 floor and a 33.6 ceiling, against Stafford's 15.87, so this is MORE POINTS. Daddy is 1-8 and starts Reggie Virgil (2.8) and Malachi Fields (7.0) at WR; Williams (13.21) and Flournoy (9.31) lift those slots by about 10.4 and 2.3. That roughly offsets the 9.2 he loses at QB. I'd use this only if the Stroud deal stalls, because both use Williams.
trades.fallback: Add McConkey as a sweetener; walk away if he wants Higgins.
trades.text: Sent you an offer, WR help for your lineup.

trades.why: Kirk Cousins averages 19.14 (20.41 last-3) with a 13.77 floor against Stafford's 15.87 and 9.12, so this is MORE RELIABLE and MORE POINTS. He is only Gavin's bench QB behind Joe Burrow (24.89). Gavin gets a usable WR depth piece in Flournoy and a similar backup in Stafford, so it costs him nothing in his lineup. I'd treat it as a fallback behind the Stroud trade.
trades.fallback: Swap Flournoy for Mayer; walk away if he wants more.

trades.why: Omar Cooper Jr. averages 15.65 (19.53 last-3) on 86% snaps and a 7.67 targets-per-game load, with a 9.88 floor. That is MORE POINTS: about +2.4 at flex over Jameson Williams' 13.21. The sample is only 4 games and he is questionable, so hold this until his status is clear. Garfy starts Chris Rodriguez Jr. (6.8) at RB, and Marks (8.86 average, 17.3 carries a game) improves that by about 2, so the deal helps him too.
trades.fallback: Drop McConkey, add Black; walk away if he adds anything.
